name: German 1st Army
summary: Outer edge of the right wing: Brussels, Mons, Le Cateau, the wheel inside Paris, the Ourcq.

name: German 2nd Army
summary: Liège, the Sambre at Charleroi, Guise, the Marne at Montmirail.

name: German 3rd Army
summary: Saxon army; the Meuse at Dinant, the marshes of Saint-Gond.

name: German 4th Army
summary: Duke Albrecht of Württemberg; the Ardennes encounter battles, the Meuse at Sedan.

name: German 5th Army
summary: Crown Prince Wilhelm; Longwy, the Ardennes, Verdun's western face.

name: German 6th Army
summary: The left wing in Lorraine: Morhange–Sarrebourg, the Trouée de Charmes, the Grand Couronné.

name: German 7th Army
summary: Josias von Heeringen; Alsace and the Vosges, then moved to the Aisne in September.

name: French 1st Army
summary: Dubail; Alsace and the Sarrebourg side of the Lorraine offensive.

name: French 2nd Army
summary: Morhange, then the defence of the Grand Couronné de Nancy.

name: French 3rd Army
summary: Ruffey, then Sarrail; the Ardennes and the Verdun hinge.

name: French 4th Army
summary: Langle de Cary; the Ardennes, the Meuse, Vitry-le-François at the Marne.

name: French 5th Army
summary: Charleroi, Guise, the retreat; under Franchet d'Espèrey from 3 September, into the gap at the Marne.

name: French 6th Army
summary: Formed around Amiens from 26 August by rail; fell back on Paris; struck Kluck on the Ourcq from 5 September.

name: French 9th Army
summary: Improvised on 29 August between the 4th and 5th Armies; held the marshes of Saint-Gond.

name: British Expeditionary Force
summary: Two corps and a cavalry division: Mons, Le Cateau, the retreat to the Grand Morin, the advance into the gap.

name: Belgian Field Army
summary: Six divisions: the Gette line, the withdrawal into Antwerp, the sorties, the Yser.
